name: The sons of Levi at the golden calf
charge: Answering, Who is on the Lord's side? and executing the sentence on their own brethren
summary: When Moses stood in the gate of the camp and asked who was on the Lord's side, all the sons of Levi gathered to him, took their swords, and went through the camp. Three thousand fell. For that day the priesthood and the service of the sanctuary were given to the tribe, and Moses' last blessing names it.
offense: Moses stood in the gate of the camp with the calf ground to powder (Exodus 32:20) and put a question rather than an order: who is on the Lord's side? The whole tribe came to him (Exodus 32:26). What they were then commanded was the hardest thing in the law, to execute the sentence on apostates without regard to kinship, slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbour (Exodus 32:27). Deuteronomy 13 states the statute they were applying, that a brother or a son or the wife of thy bosom who entices to other gods is not to be spared or concealed (Deuteronomy 33:8-11). Three thousand fell, and the account is careful that the sword did not fall on strangers.
judgment: Moses read the day as a consecration: consecrate yourselves today to the Lord, even every man upon his son and upon his brother (Exodus 32:29), that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day. The priesthood and the whole service of the sanctuary were given to the tribe (Numbers 3:31), and the Levites were taken instead of the firstborn of Israel (Numbers 3:12). Moses' final blessing on Levi names the cause exactly (Numbers 3:17), that they observed God's word and kept his covenant (Deuteronomy 33:9), and did not acknowledge their own brethren nor know their own children. Malachi holds the covenant with Levi up centuries later as what a priesthood is supposed to be (Malachi 2:4-7).

entries.commentary: When the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, they gathered unto Aaron: Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, we wot not what is become of him. Any time deliverance did not come when Israel wanted it, the nation rebelled, and Moses and the leadership got the blame; the same spirit is against the leadership of Israel to this day. Aaron said break off the golden earrings which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters. Men and women both wore earrings in the scriptures, and it is not sin. Aaron received the gold, fashioned it with a graving tool, and made a molten calf, and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. Aaron saw the miracles in Egypt and was set up as high priest, yet he succumbed to the pressure of the people; that is why the Lord chose Moses specifically to lead, because Moses could not be moved by any means. Aaron built an altar before it and made proclamation, To morrow is a feast to the LORD; and the people rose up early, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play. Israel kept provoking God, and the Lord still brought the nation into the promised land as he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

The Lord told Moses, Go, get thee down; for thy people, which thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves. They turned aside quickly out of the way, made a molten calf, worshipped it, and sacrificed thereunto. Not forty days gone, and they had already left his commandments. The spirit that was in Israel in Egypt was still in Israel when they left. It is the same coming into this truth: the evil carried in from the world will corrupt you and turn you from the Lord if it is not put off. I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people. That has been Israel's reputation with the Father from the beginning; without the laws of God we are a carnal, rebellious people, which is why these last days call for humbleness and repentance, not bringing the world's rhetoric into the congregation. Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation. Moses was of the tribe of Levi, of the seed of Jacob, so the Lord could have started over with him.

Moses besought the LORD his God: LORD, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, which thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a mighty hand? Moses had compassion and stood in the middle, interceding and mediating between the people and God. Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, and say, For mischief did he bring them out, to slay them in the mountains? And remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, to whom thou swarest by thine own self to multiply their seed as the stars of heaven, and to give the land to their seed for ever. And the LORD repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people. The Most High does not repent as a man; he has no one to answer to, he simply turned from the anger of that moment. He was never going to break his covenant, for consuming the people would have destroyed all the seed of Jacob except Moses; Moses was there to remind him of his own word. From the questions: the Lord dealt with Moses on a level where Moses could speak to him so, but the outcome stood on what was declared from the beginning; had it been his pleasure to destroy, nothing Moses said could have stayed it.

Moses went down from the mount with the two tables of the testimony in his hand, written on both their sides; the tables were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, graven upon the tables. Joshua heard the noise of the people and said, There is a noise of war in the camp; Moses answered, It is not the voice of them that shout for mastery, neither the voice of them that cry for being overcome, but the noise of them that sing do I hear. They were feasting and dancing around the idol. Joshua's loyalty at the mount is one of the main reasons the Lord chose him to succeed Moses. As soon as he came nigh unto the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, Moses' anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands and brake them beneath the mount. He took the calf which they had made, burnt it in the fire, ground it to powder, strawed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it. Our forefathers were no joke about the law; Nehemiah likewise put hands on those who profaned the sabbath in his day.

Moses said unto Aaron, What did this people unto thee, that thou hast brought so great a sin upon them? He had left Aaron in charge, and came back to a camp deep in wickedness. Aaron answered, Let not the anger of my lord wax hot: thou knowest the people, that they are set on mischief; they said make us gods, I cast the gold into the fire, and there came out this calf. A leader cannot blame the congregation, the same excuse Saul gave; the charge has to be carried. The psalm gives the depth of it: they soon forgat his works and waited not for his counsel, they made a calf in Horeb and changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass, and they forgat God their saviour, which had done great things in Egypt, wondrous works in the land of Ham, and terrible things by the Red sea.

The people were naked, for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies. That is the same nakedness of [Genesis 3](/bible/genesis/3), the shame of sin uncovered. Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, Who is on the LORD's side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him. Every man put his sword by his side and went in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men. The Lord chose those particular ones to die; that spirit would have wrecked the nation down the road, so he moved it out of the congregation. Do not be broken when someone leaves the truth; the Lord moves spiritually. Consecrate yourselves to day to the LORD, even every man upon his son, and upon his brother, that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day.

Moses said unto the people, Ye have sinned a great sin. They had broken the first two commandments just given at Sinai: no other gods before him, and no graven image to bow down to and serve. Moses returned unto the LORD to mediate: yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written. That is a real leader, putting himself in the way of harm for his people. The Lord answered, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book; therefore now go, lead the people, and mine Angel shall go before thee; nevertheless in the day when I visit I will visit their sin upon them. And the LORD plagued the people, because they made the calf, which Aaron made.

This is the blessing wherewith Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel before his death. This chapter is prophetic concerning who the tribes would be in the last days: the blessings point to where you can examine history and identify each tribe. The Lord came from Sinai and shined forth from mount Paran, and came with ten thousands of saints; from his right hand went a fiery law for them. Moses commanded us a law, even the inheritance of the congregation of Jacob: the laws of the Most High are our inheritance. And he was king in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people and the tribes of Israel were gathered together.

Let Reuben live, and not die; and let not his men be few. Reuben is the Seminole Indians: under Andrew Jackson the Indian removal campaign set out to exterminate them, and many were slaughtered, but they were not able to kill them all. They tried it, but they were not fully successful; that is why the blessing says let Reuben live, and not die.

Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people: let his hands be sufficient for him; and be thou an help to him from his enemies. The Most High said we would be scattered into the four corners and the nations would conspire that we not remember who we are; but he wakes Judah first. Judah, the so-called blacks in America, are the first to remember that they are the Israelites, and once Judah learns who they are, they go and teach the other tribes scattered throughout the four corners; that is bring him unto his people. That is why Judah is at the forefront of this work. The gates of hell will try to prevail against the quest to wake up the twelve tribes, but the Most High is a help to Judah from his enemies to fulfill that mission.

And of Levi he said, Let thy Thummim and thy Urim be with thy holy one. The Urim and the Thummim were worn in the garment of the high priest, as [Exodus 28](/bible/exodus/28) lays out; that pertains to the Levites, the lineage of Aaron, whom thou didst prove at Massah, and with whom thou didst strive at the waters of Meribah, in [Exodus 17](/bible/exodus/17). Who said unto his father and to his mother, I have not seen him; neither did he acknowledge his brethren, nor knew his own children: for they have observed thy word, and kept thy covenant. This is the zeal Levi had for the Most High. At the golden calf, when Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, Who is on the Lord's side? let him come unto me, only the sons of Levi gathered themselves unto him. They took every man his sword and did according to the word of Moses without hesitating, and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men. That is why the blessing says they saw not father or mother nor acknowledged their brethren: that is the devotion they had for the covenant.

They shall teach Jacob thy judgments, and Israel thy law: they shall put incense before thee, and whole burnt sacrifice upon thine altar. This is the office the Most High gave Levi, and in particular the high priest. Aaron was chosen out of all men living to offer sacrifices, incense, and a sweet savour, to make reconciliation for the people, and that office pertained to his lineage: to teach Jacob the testimonies and inform Israel in his laws. That is why Levi had no land of their own but dwelt among all the tribes of Israel: they were responsible for making the sacrifices and teaching the laws to the people.

Bless, Lord, his substance, and accept the work of his hands. His substance goes into the tithes that Levi would receive, and the work of his hands goes into the freewill offerings brought forth to the Lord. Smite through the loins of them that rise against him, and of them that hate him, that they rise not again. In history you see it in the Haitian revolution under Toussaint Louverture: they smote through the loins of them that hated them. Levi was about that action to a magnitude the other tribes never matched. That they rise not again is ultimately fulfilled when Christ returns.

And of Benjamin he said, The beloved of the Lord shall dwell in safety by him. Dwelling in safety means Benjamin would not be killed off in slavery. The Lord shall cover him all the day long, and he shall dwell between his shoulders: between the shoulders of the Lord represents the skies and the earth, going into the good climate and the good land they would have.

And of Joseph he said, Blessed of the Lord be his land. Joseph is Ephraim and Manasseh: Joseph was one of the twelve sons of Jacob, but Jacob put his name on Joseph's two sons, so his grandsons make up two tribes of Israel; when we read of Joseph we are reading of Ephraim and Manasseh. The precious things of heaven refer to the good weather on their land, and the dew and the deep that coucheth beneath go into the seas whose benefits they reap. The precious fruits brought forth by the sun are the crops their land grows: mango, papaya, avocado, pineapple, coconut, banana, sugar cane, fruits you cannot grow in north Florida. The precious things put forth by the moon go into the coqui, a frog species that exists only in Puerto Rico and comes out at night with its distinct call. The chief things of the ancient mountains are the diamonds, gold, and silver in their land, and the precious things of the lasting hills include the coffee beans that come out of their hills. Let the blessing come upon the head of Joseph, him that was separated from his brethren. Ephraim said, Yet I am become rich: hence the very name Puerto Rico, the port of riches. But like we read earlier, they waxed fat and became prideful as well.

His glory is like the firstling of his bullock: as in the law that sanctified the firstborn unto the Most High, that is the glory of the birthright given to Joseph. His horns are like the horns of unicorns: two horns, Ephraim and Manasseh. With them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth: the Most High used Ephraim and Manasseh as the heads to push the ten tribes over to this side of the world, as the account of the tribes taking counsel to go forth into a further country shows. And they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh: the blessing on Jacob's grandsons was to grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth. The Most High gets geographic with it: they went from the east to the west and multiplied in the midst of the hemisphere, in Central America.

And of Zebulun he said, Rejoice, Zebulun, in thy going out; and, Issachar, in thy tents. Notice the grouping: Zebulun and Issachar are blessed together because they would dwell very close, with linked cities at their borders. They shall call the people unto the mountain; there they shall offer sacrifices of righteousness. In the promised land they linked up to make sacrifices of righteousness; but when they linked up on this side of the world as the Aztecs and the Mayans, they erected pyramids and eventually went off and sacrificed to other gods, even human sacrifice, as Hosea testifies of their sacrificing. For they shall suck of the abundance of the seas, and of treasures hid in the sand: the gold and silver discovered in their land, which is why the conquistadors were so glad to stumble upon it.

And of Gad he said, Blessed be he that enlargeth Gad. Gad alone holds over three hundred Indian tribes within itself; it is a very large tribe. He dwelleth as a lion, and teareth the arm with the crown of the head: Gad was a warlike, predator people, and the tearing of the arm goes into the blood brother pact they were known for making, the chief with the crown of feathers having a man tear his arm to be accepted into the tribe. And he provided the first part for himself: that is North America, the mainland, the largest and best portion. Because there, in a portion of the lawgiver, was he seated: the tribe of Gad served as the lawgivers for the northern kingdom. And he came with the heads of the people: the travel to this side of the earth was made with Ephraim and Manasseh, the horns, at the head, dealing with the so-called Hispanics and Indians together. He executed the justice of the Lord, and his judgments with Israel, before they went off.

And of Dan he said, Dan is a lion's whelp: he shall leap from Bashan. Dan is a warlike people; the Carib Indians did not play. He shall leap from Bashan says a lot in a short verse: Bashan was in the most northern part of Israel, so leaping from Bashan lands Dan in the middle of all Israel. That is why Dan today is not their own tribe but is absorbed into all the other tribes, primarily Benjamin, dwelling in the Caribbean. Amos says they shall fall, and never rise up again: Dan fell and never rose again as a tribe, which is why Dan is not mentioned among the tribes of the 144,000 in [Revelation 7](/bible/revelation/7). And as [Genesis 49](/bible/genesis/49) says, Dan is an adder in the path: look how the islands are shaped geographically, like a serpent.

And of Naphtali he said, O Naphtali, satisfied with favour: Naphtali is Argentina and Chile today. Satisfied with favour goes into the grapes they are able to produce in their land for wine, and coffee as well. And full with the blessing of the Lord: to this day their land is rich with agriculture and cattle. Possess thou the west and the south: the Most High gets geographic again. Look at a map of the world: what land sits in the southwestern region of the earth? Argentina and Chile. Stop playing with the prophets; we know who we are.

And of Asher he said, Let Asher be blessed with children. Asher is also a large tribe: the countries that make up Asher today include Brazil, Peru, Colombia, and Uruguay, and Brazil has the largest population of children in the world. Let him be acceptable to his brethren: for a period of time they became so wild in their ways that they were not acceptable in the sight of their brethren. And let him dip his foot in oil: one of the largest outputs of crude oil resources is Colombia. Thy shoes shall be iron and brass: the Hebrew word for iron is barzel; say it fast and you hear Brazil. It goes into the mineral resources in that land, iron, copper, zinc. And as thy days, so shall thy strength be.

There is none like unto the God of Jeshurun, who rideth upon the heaven in thy help. The eternal God is thy refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms: he shall thrust out the enemy from before thee. Notice how the song and blessing have evolved: from Israel provoking the Most High and being punished, the teeth of beasts sent upon us, now it goes into our salvation, how the Most High will be our refuge. Israel then shall dwell in safety alone. Happy art thou, O Israel: who is like unto thee, O people saved by the Lord! And thine enemies shall be found liars unto thee: after all these years of the crafty counsel, being told you are anything but Israel and that everybody else holds your heritage, the Most High said your enemies shall be found liars, and thou shalt tread upon their high places. Never trust your enemy: your enemy will do everything in his power to keep you oppressed and subject to him, including lying to you about your history. As in the days of the Maccabees, the leaders show the people the falsehood of the heathen and the breach of their oaths, the covenants and treaties they broke with our people; after so long you learn that your enemies have been liars this whole time.

Aaron and his sons were appointed to wait on the priest's office, and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. Anybody outside the tribe of Levi, when it came to doing the service of the Lord, was considered a stranger.

The Most High took the Levites from among the children of Israel instead of all the firstborn that openeth the matrix. The matrix is the womb; that is what the Lord calls it. All the firstborn are his from the day he smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt. Verse 13 proves the Most High does not love everybody; he killed all the firstborn of Egypt.

The children of Levi were numbered after the houses of their fathers, by their families. Your lineage is determined by your father, not your mother. The claim that identity passes through the mother is nowhere in the Bible; number the children of Levi after the house of their fathers is the standard of scripture.

Of Gershon were the families of the Libnites and the Shimites, numbered 7,500 males from a month old and upward, and they pitched behind the tabernacle westward. Depending on your family lineage you had a specific side of the tabernacle that you and all your descendants had to be on. The charge of the sons of Gershon was the tabernacle and the tent, the covering thereof, the hanging for the door, the hangings of the court, and the cords of it; that was their responsibility.

The ending "ites" denotes the people of; the Kohathites are the people of Kohath. They numbered 8,600 and pitched on the side of the tabernacle southward. Their charge was the ark, the table, the candlestick, the altars, and the vessels of the sanctuary. Only they were responsible for the ark; anybody outside of that suffered the judgment of the Most High, as Uzzah did generations later when he put forth his hand to the ark and God smote him on the spot.
Eleazar the son of Aaron was chief over the chief of the Levites, with the oversight of them that keep the charge of the sanctuary. He was the manager of the tabernacle.

Of Merari were the families of the Mahlites and the Mushites, numbered 6,200, and they pitched on the side of the tabernacle northward. Their custody and charge was the boards of the tabernacle, the bars, the pillars, the sockets, the vessels, and the pillars of the court round about with their sockets, pins, and cords.

Moses and Aaron and his sons encamped before the tabernacle toward the east, keeping the charge of the sanctuary; and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. Anybody outside the tribe of Levi that approached unto the tabernacle was considered a stranger.

All the Levites numbered from a month old and upward were 22,000; the Most High was separating the tribe of Levi unto himself instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel. The firstborn males of the children of Israel were twenty and two thousand two hundred and threescore and thirteen. A score is twenty, so threescore and thirteen is 73; the count is 22,273.

The firstborn of Israel outnumbered the Levites by 273, and those odd ones were redeemed at five shekels apiece by the poll, after the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs. Moses took the redemption money, 1,365 shekels, and gave it unto Aaron and to his sons. The money went to Aaron and the priests because they had to take care of the widows, the fatherless, and the strangers; the strangers are our people that come from different parts of the land down to Jerusalem needing help. That is how the Most High put money into the sanctuary to take care of those that could not take care of themselves.

The prophet or dreamer of dreams who speaks to turn you away from the Lord your God was put to death under the kingdom. Today Israel is in the land of its oppressors and cannot exact that judgment, and no kind of violence is advocated; the deceived and the deceiver are his, and the judgment belongs to the Most High. What is done today: mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned, and avoid them. The doctrine learned is the law, for I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law. Going contrary to the laws of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, or of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you, and secretly enticing others to follow, is how one turns people away from the Lord; those men and those women have to be put out from among the body.

If thy brother, thy son, thy daughter, the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend which is as thine own soul entice thee secretly to serve other gods: these are the people closest to you, the ones that can have influence on you. Thou shalt not consent, nor hearken, nor pity, nor spare, neither shalt thou conceal him, meaning hide him; when wickedness is concealed, the whole nation is put in jeopardy. Trust in a person is no cover for your soul: when someone you love and trust has the devil on them, they will lead you astray. Nobody can make you do anything, but they can influence you; do not give anyone that credit and let them cause you to lose your crown. This is why [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1) is opened at the start of class: if you know of anything, you are supposed to utter it. Many grew up on snitches get stitches, but in repentance we have to understand that concealing sin is part of why Israel is in the condition it is in, and we have to teach righteousness. It is that simple.

If certain men, the children of Belial, withdraw the inhabitants of a city, saying, let us go and serve other gods: inquire, make search, and ask diligently, and if it be truth and the thing certain, that city was smitten with the edge of the sword, gathered into the midst of the street, and burnt with fire, an heap for ever, not to be built again. Achan is the example of this kind of judgment: Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing, and one man's folly kindled the anger of the Lord against all Israel. Wars Israel had been winning without losing a man began to be lost, and Joshua had to search and seek out who had committed the crime in Israel. All Israel stoned Achan with stones and burned him with fire in the valley of Achor, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; righteous judgment lifted the wrath and the people were able to move forward.

verses.text: And when Moses saw that the people were naked; (for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies:)
Then Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and said, Who is on the Lord’s side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him.

And he said unto them, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Put every man his sword by his side, and go in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbour.
And the children of Levi did according to the word of Moses: and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men.
For Moses had said, Consecrate yourselves to day to the Lord, even every man upon his son, and upon his brother; that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day.
And of Levi he said, Let thy Thummim and thy Urim be with thy holy one, whom thou didst prove at Massah, and with whom thou didst strive at the waters of Meribah;
Who said unto his father and to his mother, I have not seen him; neither did he acknowledge his brethren, nor knew his own children: for they have observed thy word, and kept thy covenant.
They shall teach Jacob thy judgments, and Israel thy law: they shall put incense before thee, and whole burnt sacrifice upon thine altar.
Bless, Lord, his substance, and accept the work of his hands: smite through the loins of them that rise against him, and of them that hate him, that they rise not again.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
And I, behold, I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel instead of all the firstborn that openeth the matrix among the children of Israel: therefore the Levites shall be mine;

Because all the firstborn are mine; for on the day that I smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt I hallowed unto me all the firstborn in Israel, both man and beast: mine shall they be: I am the Lord.
And the Lord said unto Moses, Number all the firstborn of the males of the children of Israel from a month old and upward, and take the number of their names.

And thou shalt take the Levites for me (I am the Lord) instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel; and the cattle of the Levites instead of all the firstlings among the cattle of the children of Israel.
And Moses numbered, as the Lord commanded him, all the firstborn among the children of Israel.
And all the firstborn males by the number of names, from a month old and upward, of those that were numbered of them, were twenty and two thousand two hundred and threescore and thirteen.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
Take the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel, and the cattle of the Levites instead of their cattle; and the Levites shall be mine: I am the Lord.
And ye shall know that I have sent this commandment unto you, that my covenant might be with Levi, saith the Lord of hosts.
My covenant was with him of life and peace; and I gave them to him for the fear wherewith he feared me, and was afraid before my name.
The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked with me in peace and equity, and did turn many away from iniquity.
For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.

If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which thou hast not known, thou, nor thy fathers;
Namely, of the gods of the people which are round about you, nigh unto thee, or far off from thee, from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth;
Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him; neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare, neither shalt thou conceal him:
But thou shalt surely kill him; thine hand shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterwards the hand of all the people.
And thou shalt stone him with stones, that he die; because he hath sought to thrust thee away from the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.
And all Israel shall hear, and fear, and shall do no more any such wickedness as this is among you.

text.text: And when Moses saw that the people were naked; (for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies:)
Then Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and said, Who is on the Lord’s side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him.

And he said unto them, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Put every man his sword by his side, and go in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbour.
And the children of Levi did according to the word of Moses: and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men.
For Moses had said, Consecrate yourselves to day to the Lord, even every man upon his son, and upon his brother; that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day.
And of Levi he said, Let thy Thummim and thy Urim be with thy holy one, whom thou didst prove at Massah, and with whom thou didst strive at the waters of Meribah;
Who said unto his father and to his mother, I have not seen him; neither did he acknowledge his brethren, nor knew his own children: for they have observed thy word, and kept thy covenant.
They shall teach Jacob thy judgments, and Israel thy law: they shall put incense before thee, and whole burnt sacrifice upon thine altar.
Bless, Lord, his substance, and accept the work of his hands: smite through the loins of them that rise against him, and of them that hate him, that they rise not again.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
And I, behold, I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel instead of all the firstborn that openeth the matrix among the children of Israel: therefore the Levites shall be mine;

Because all the firstborn are mine; for on the day that I smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt I hallowed unto me all the firstborn in Israel, both man and beast: mine shall they be: I am the Lord.
And the Lord said unto Moses, Number all the firstborn of the males of the children of Israel from a month old and upward, and take the number of their names.

And thou shalt take the Levites for me (I am the Lord) instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel; and the cattle of the Levites instead of all the firstlings among the cattle of the children of Israel.
And Moses numbered, as the Lord commanded him, all the firstborn among the children of Israel.
And all the firstborn males by the number of names, from a month old and upward, of those that were numbered of them, were twenty and two thousand two hundred and threescore and thirteen.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
Take the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel, and the cattle of the Levites instead of their cattle; and the Levites shall be mine: I am the Lord.
And ye shall know that I have sent this commandment unto you, that my covenant might be with Levi, saith the Lord of hosts.
My covenant was with him of life and peace; and I gave them to him for the fear wherewith he feared me, and was afraid before my name.
The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked with me in peace and equity, and did turn many away from iniquity.
For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.

If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which thou hast not known, thou, nor thy fathers;
Namely, of the gods of the people which are round about you, nigh unto thee, or far off from thee, from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth;
Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him; neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare, neither shalt thou conceal him:
But thou shalt surely kill him; thine hand shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterwards the hand of all the people.
And thou shalt stone him with stones, that he die; because he hath sought to thrust thee away from the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.
And all Israel shall hear, and fear, and shall do no more any such wickedness as this is among you.
